goals: mechanistic: estimate field-scale nitrate LEACHING FLUX and recharge below the root zone as a function of land use and soil, per column
validation: relate simulated leaching source strength to external well nitrate records (indirect / regional only — see feasibility)
key_processes: soil nitrogen cycling and nitrate leaching (ELM CN)
NOT representable: lateral saturated transport, reactive attenuation (denitrification), well-screen mixing

model_choice.rationale: ELM's CN biogeochemistry can produce a per-column nitrate leaching flux + recharge under land-use and soil contrasts. It CANNOT transport that nitrate laterally to a well; the well-arrival concentration is out of scope for the single-column stack.
model_choice.coupling_note: Estimating arrival concentration would require ELM leaching-flux/recharge to drive a PFLOTRAN (or equivalent) reactive-transport aquifer model with lateral flow. The ELM->PFLOTRAN coupler is not implemented, and PFLOTRAN as available solves steady-state flow only — no reactive solute transport / denitrification. Listed in requires_capabilities.

answerable: field-scale nitrate leaching flux below the root zone as a function of land use and soil (given spin-up + WTD warm start + verified N-leaching output)
recharge / sub-surface drainage (QDRAI) per column that would serve as a transport source term

not_answerable.aspect: arrival concentration of nitrate at drinking-water wells
not_answerable.why: single-column ELM has no lateral transport and no regional water table; there is no path from a field column to a well. Reactive solute transport and well mixing are not represented at all.
not_answerable.needs: reactive lateral groundwater transport model + ELM->transport coupler

not_answerable.aspect: denitrification / attenuation of nitrate along the flow path
not_answerable.why: no saturated-zone reactive transport capability; PFLOTRAN as provided is steady-state flow only

not_answerable.aspect: travel time / breakthrough timing from field to well
not_answerable.why: requires lateral advective transport and aquifer geometry the stack cannot represent
not_answerable.needs: coupled transient aquifer transport model with lateral flow

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (land use x soil drainage class)
sampling_strategy.n_justification: The mechanism the stack CAN resolve (leaching source strength) is controlled by land use x soil. 3 land-use classes x 2 drainage classes = 6 cells; the two dominant fertilized-row-crop cells get light replication (+2) because they are the source of concern. This spans the leaching drivers without a blind dense grid. Elevation is NOT a stratifier (160 m relief, not the mechanism).
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Concentrate columns on fertilized row-crop areas over contrasting soils (well-drained vs poorly-drained/tile-prone), since these dominate nitrate loading. Downstream expander samples SSURGO drainage class and a land-use raster to place points; no coordinates invented here.
sampling_strategy.replication: 2 extra columns in the fertilized-row-crop strata to capture soil-driven spread in the highest-loading class.

sampling_plan.reason: dominant nitrate source over freely-draining soil — high vertical leaching flux expected
dominant source over soils where tile drainage strongly routes nitrate — key loading contrast
background leaching over wet soil, closes the 3x2 stratification

validation_design.target_variable: nitrate leaching flux / recharge (ELM source term)
validation_design.comparison: indirect/regional ONLY — well records are concentrations at the well AFTER lateral transport + attenuation, which the stack does not simulate. At best a qualitative check that high-leaching land-use/soil strata coincide with elevated observed well nitrate. NOT a co-located flux validation.
validation_design.metric: qualitative rank/consistency (no quantitative bias/RMSE is defensible without a transport model)
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on well-record density; but not directly comparable to model output

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline NLDAS forcing, native SSURGO soil, ELM CN nitrogen cycle on, WTD warm start + spin-up

requires_capabilities.capability: reactive lateral groundwater transport model + ELM->transport coupler
requires_capabilities.why: the entire deliverable (nitrate arriving at a well) requires lateral advective transport of the ELM leaching flux through the aquifer
requires_capabilities.blocks: arrival concentration at wells; travel-time estimates

requires_capabilities.why: nitrate is attenuated along the saturated flow path; PFLOTRAN as provided is steady-state flow only
must confirm nitrate leaching flux is emitted as a history field for the CN model
to stratify columns by land use and set fertilizer N inputs
drainage class is a first-order control on leaching vs tile routing
recharge and leaching are slow states; cold-start artifacts otherwise
to attempt any (even indirect) comparison and to site future transport receptors

assumptions: The intended deliverable (well arrival concentration) is treated as out-of-scope for the current stack; the design is scoped down to leaching-flux/recharge source-term estimation.
ELM CN nitrogen cycle is enabled and its leaching flux is a meaningful output for the region.
Land-use and SSURGO drainage-class rasters exist for HUC 07060002 for the downstream expander.
External well nitrate records are point concentrations at wells, not leaching-flux measurements.
Elevation relief (160 m) is not a controlling driver for this question and is not stratified on.
open_questions: Are fertilizer application rates / management schedules available to parameterize N inputs per land-use class?
Do the well nitrate records include location and screen depth, so future coupled transport could define receptors?
Is there interest in the (feasible) leaching-flux source-term product as a standalone deliverable, pending the transport coupler?
Is aquifer geometry / hydraulic property data available to eventually build the PFLOTRAN transport domain?
